ruling.recommended_action: Pay rider a $5.54 voucher (3.93 km × $1.4098/km) for the unexempt detour on this RydeTAXI trip; no account flag (driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat is a polite route-arrangement request ("ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?") and "Sure, go ahead." — a pickup/routing arrangement, no threat, abuse, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in the complaint, chat or driver statement. safety_concern = none.

Route: one off-route segment, F3 (12:29–12:39, 6.34 km driven where the optimal route covers 3.07 km, +3.27 km, up to 755 m off route). Review under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

Driver's justification is traffic (F11), but RD-4 requires a traffic fact tied to the replaced optimal segment: F14 records no incidents at all, and the only band evidence is F12 (PIE band 2, 12:04–12:29). Two problems: (i) RD-4(b) says a band fact alone does not exempt in the MVP (gap G3) — it is only corroboration for an incident under (a); (ii) F12's window ends 12:29, i.e. at the moment the detour begins, so it does not cover the driven segment. So RD-4 does not exempt F3.

RD-5 consent was raised in the chat before the deviation, so I must read its scope. F8/F9 is a specific-road agreement ("go round via Sims Avenue"), but nothing in the record ties the driven segment to Sims Avenue: the only route-name facts are F12/F13 (PIE and Central Expressway), both in the negative sense — they say nothing about Sims Avenue; the segment itself just shows 755 m away from the optimal route with no road name. Timing alone cannot tie it (G13), and there is no message placing the car on Sims Avenue. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the finding is undetermined, not "counts". Per RD-5/G13 an undetermined finding that affects the amount goes to a person — but here the amount is unaffected whether the segment is counted or exempt: the billed excess is the same $5.54 either way (see below), so the undetermined finding does not change the outcome and no escalation is required on that account.

Amount: RD-2 / RD-1 violation. The driver deviated without a qualifying excuse, so the extra distance billed is not the driver's to keep. F4 bills $5.54 (3.93 km × $1.4098/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km). The complaint claims "more than the estimate"; on this RydeTAXI trip the metered overage attributable to the detour is 3.27 km (F3) and the billed excess-distance line is 3.93 km (F4) — the record does not break down the further 0.66 km, so on the evidence actually provided the whole excess-distance item of $5.54 is the overcharge the rider can have refunded. Rejecting the rider's broader framing: the rest of the fare (base, time, platform fee, the 0.4 min waiting charge under RD-3(c)/F5, which on RydeTAXI is metered waiting and is non-refundable) is properly charged; the fixed-quote analysis of RD-2 does not apply since RydeTAXI is metered.

RD-6: not triggered — driver's F17 shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route, so route_disputes_upheld_90d < 1; no flag_account.

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the rider's only pre-detour consent is a named-road agreement, 'go round via Sims Avenue' (F8/F9, timestamped F10). Nothing in the record ties the driven segment to Sims Avenue — the only road-name facts are F12/F13 (PIE, Central Expressway) and the driver's statement F11 is a claim, not consent (G11); timing alone does not tie the segment to the road (G13), and no record places the segment elsewhere. Hence named_road_untied → undetermined, not exempt. RD-4 traffic defence also fails (F14 no incidents; F12 alone cannot exempt, G3) so the finding does not become exempt on that ground either. The undetermined finding does not change the amount (the billed excess-distance item F4 is $5.54 whether or not this segment is counted), so no escalation results.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's after-the-fact statement that the rider agreed is a claim, not consent; consent must be the rider's own pre-detour message (G11). The rider's pre-detour chat (F8/F9) is a named-road agreement that, on this record, is not tied to the driven segment (G13).

Traffic band on PIE is band 2, but no incident on the replaced optimal segment is recorded (F14) and its window ends 12:29, when the detour starts — RD-4(b) alone does not exempt (G3), so the RD-4 reasonable-cause defence is not made out.
The $0.11 waiting charge is metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is non-refundable (RD-3(c)); no ground to waive it.

ruling.evidence_gap: The record does not break the billed 3.93 km excess distance (F4) down into the 3.27 km measured detour (F3) and the remaining ~0.66 km, nor give a road name for the driven segment; the reward is therefore computed on the billed excess-distance item as a whole.
